citations.claim: Energy at first violating step exceeds allowed limit, showing net energy gain with no controller work
Initial energy baseline before any bounce
Energy already climbing mid-run showing progressive gain across bounces

counterfactual.change: Changed only bodies[0].e from 1.0 to 0.0; inelastic impacts dissipate the per-bounce energy injection so total energy stays below initial and no energy_bound violation occurs.

explanation: Single ball dropped from rest near floor with e=1, gravity 14.78, dt~0.0207 bounces repeatedly. No controller work. Energy rises monotonically across bounces (E0~139.9 to ~157.9 at step 90 to ~158.9 at step 94). Likely cause is contact solver adding energy on nominally elastic impacts: impulse plus positional correction applied while gravity injects momentum during substeps, and semi-implicit Euler integration does not conserve energy, so each bounce returns slightly more mechanical energy than it had, accumulating beyond 10%+5J tolerance over ~94 steps.
vision_note: The single ball remains low near the floor from steps 91 to 94 with almost no frame-to-frame change in height. No escape, tunneling, or explosive jump is visible; the energy growth is not apparent as dramatic motion.
